translations.team.title: Who you are talking to
translations.team.body: IDEM has two co-founders. Both are engineers, both are Cameroonian, and both answer their own email.
translations.team.arolle.bio: Senior software engineer. She decides what IDEM builds and what it refuses to build, and she knows the African entrepreneurial ecosystem from the inside.
translations.team.romuald.bio: DevSecOps engineer. He owns the infrastructure, the security of the platform and everything that has to keep running when traffic grows.
translations.video-trailer.simple_description: Watch how we transform ideas into complete applications
translations.about-page.hero.lede: Two engineers from Cameroon, one platform, and a single conviction: an entrepreneur in Yaoundé should not pay four times more than one in Paris for the same work.
translations.about-page.commitments.title: What we hold to
translations.about-page.commitments.body: World-class tools cost what a developer in San Francisco earns in an hour. That is the barrier. Everything below exists to lower it.
translations.about-page.values.title: Five words we are held to
translations.about-page.journey.title: One rung at a time
translations.about-page.vision.title: One million businesses that actually pay their founder
translations.about-page.vision.body: Not a million accounts created. A million African businesses that earn money, by 2035. That is the only figure we measure ourselves against.
translations.about-page.contact.title: Talk to us directly
translations.about-page.commitments.free.title: Start without paying
translations.about-page.commitments.free.description: Describe your project, see every deliverable, pay only for what you keep. No card asked for.
translations.about-page.commitments.price.title: Priced for the continent
translations.about-page.commitments.price.description: Three to five times below the international platforms, billed in CFA francs, paid by Mobile Money.
translations.about-page.commitments.open.title: Readable, forkable, yours
translations.about-page.commitments.open.description: The whole codebase is public, under Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause. Audit it, run it on your own machine, deliver client work with it. Reselling IDEM itself is the one thing it rules out.
translations.about-page.values.sovereignty.title: African sovereignty
translations.about-page.values.sovereignty.descriptio: Every technical choice is weighed against one question: who keeps control of the code and the data.
translations.about-page.values.discipline.title: Discipline
translations.about-page.values.discipline.description: We ship what works. A feature that cannot be explained in one sentence is not finished.
translations.about-page.values.passion.title: Passion
translations.about-page.values.passion.description: We build for the entrepreneurs we grew up around, and we use the platform for our own company.
translations.about-page.values.patience.title: Patience
translations.about-page.values.patience.description: Infrastructure takes years. We would rather be solid in five years than loud this quarter.
translations.about-page.values.perseverance.title: Perseverance
translations.about-page.values.perseverance.descripti: Power cuts, payment rails, bandwidth. The obstacles are known, and none of them is a reason to stop.
translations.about-page.milestones.foundation.title: IDEM is founded in Douala
translations.about-page.milestones.foundation.descrip: Two co-founders, one question: why does a Cameroonian entrepreneur pay four times more for the same tooling?
translations.about-page.milestones.mvp.title: First public version
translations.about-page.milestones.mvp.description: Brand identity, business plan, website and go-live, generated end to end from a single description.
translations.about-page.milestones.openSource.title: The codebase goes public
translations.about-page.milestones.openSource.descrip: Everything released under Apache 2.0, with self-hosting documented so nobody depends on us to keep running.
translations.about-page.milestones.expansion.title: Hosting on the continent
translations.about-page.milestones.expansion.descript: Data centres and payment partners country by country, so latency and currency stop being obstacles.
translations.african-market-page.hero.lede: Africa has the youngest population on earth and the highest rate of people starting a business. What it does not have is tooling priced for it. That is the whole gap IDEM works in.
translations.african-market-page.figures.title: The market, in six numbers
translations.african-market-page.figures.sources: Sources: GSMA Mobile Economy Sub-Saharan Africa, ITU, Partech Africa Tech Venture Capital Report, IFC.
translations.african-market-page.why.title: Why here, why now
translations.african-market-page.why.body: None of this is a forecast. Mobile money, the median age and the number of registered small businesses are all measured today.
translations.african-market-page.difference.title: What an imported platform gets wrong
translations.african-market-page.difference.lede: The problem is rarely the model. It is the price, the currency, the payment rail and the assumption that your customers read English.
translations.african-market-page.rollout.title: Region by region
translations.african-market-page.rollout.payments: A region counts as open when you can pay from it. Mobile Money is live in thirteen countries; the rest follow their operators.
translations.african-market-page.cta.title: Your turn
translations.african-market-page.cta.body: Describe your business in a few sentences and see the brand, the plan and the site it produces. Nothing to pay to find out.
translations.african-market-page.stat.population.desc: Median age nineteen — the youngest population of any continent, heading for 2.5 billion by 2050.
translations.african-market-page.stat.internet.label: Internet users
translations.african-market-page.stat.internet.descri: Growing about ten percent a year, and overwhelmingly on a phone rather than a desktop.
translations.african-market-page.stat.smes.label: Small businesses
translations.african-market-page.stat.smes.descriptio: They account for roughly eighty percent of employment on the continent.
translations.african-market-page.stat.mobileMoney.des: Africa carries more mobile money traffic than the rest of the world put together.
translations.african-market-page.stat.entrepreneurshi: The highest rate of new business creation measured anywhere.
translations.african-market-page.stat.startups.label: Tech companies
translations.african-market-page.stat.startups.descri: Active across the continent, three times the count of 2020.
translations.african-market-page.reason.mobile.title: The phone is the computer
translations.african-market-page.reason.mobile.descri: Products designed desktop-first lose most of the market on the first screen. Everything in IDEM is built to be used from a phone.
translations.african-market-page.reason.mobile.eviden: More than eight in ten connections are mobile.
translations.african-market-page.reason.payment.title: Payment is the real barrier
translations.african-market-page.reason.payment.descr: A card-only checkout stops most would-be customers before the first screen. Topping up a wallet by Mobile Money does not.
translations.african-market-page.reason.payment.evide: Mobile Money live in thirteen countries, billed in CFA francs.
translations.african-market-page.reason.young.title: A generation starting out
translations.african-market-page.reason.young.descrip: Sixty percent of the continent is under twenty-five, and the people entering the workforce are the ones creating the businesses.
translations.african-market-page.reason.young.evidenc: Around 200 million young people join the workforce by 2035.
translations.african-market-page.reason.sovereignty.d: When the tool, the hosting and the invoice all sit abroad, every price rise and every policy change lands on the entrepreneur.
translations.african-market-page.reason.sovereignty.e: Apache 2.0, self-hostable, data exportable at any time.
translations.african-market-page.advantage.price.desc: Every country has its own grid, built from local purchasing power rather than converted from a single currency.
translations.african-market-page.advantage.payment.de: MTN and Orange Mobile Money top up the wallet, and the wallet pays for what you generate.
translations.african-market-page.advantage.language.d: French, English and Portuguese today. The deliverables follow the language of your request, not the language of the site.
translations.african-market-page.advantage.accounting: Financial statements follow the SYSCOHADA chart of accounts, so a loan officer in Abidjan or Douala can read them.
translations.african-market-page.advantage.sovereignt: Deploy to managed hosting, to your own VPS, or to a machine in your office. The choice stays yours.
translations.african-market-page.advantage.open.title: A platform you can audit
translations.african-market-page.advantage.open.descr: African developers can read the code, fix it and run it. That is what sovereignty means in practice.
translations.african-market-page.region.central.name: Central Africa
translations.african-market-page.region.central.descr: Our home market. We know the registry, the tax calendar and the banks because we went through them ourselves.
translations.african-market-page.region.central.count: Cameroon, Gabon, Congo, Chad, Central African Republic
translations.african-market-page.region.west.name: West Africa
translations.african-market-page.region.west.descript: The largest tech market on the continent, and the one where Mobile Money coverage is deepest.
translations.african-market-page.region.west.countrie: Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Benin, Togo, Mali, Burkina Faso
translations.african-market-page.region.east.name: East Africa
translations.african-market-page.region.east.descript: The platform works today; what remains is a payment agreement with each operator so you can top up locally.
translations.african-market-page.region.south.name: Southern Africa
translations.african-market-page.region.south.descrip: The most mature infrastructure on the continent, and the market where we compete head-on with international platforms.
translations.african-market-page.region.south.countri: South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Zambia, Zimbabwe

translations.contact-page.hero.lede: A question about the platform, a quote for your company, a partnership: write to us and a founder reads it. Replies go out within one working day.
translations.contact-page.form.title: Write to us
translations.contact-page.form.body: Tell us what you are building and where you are stuck. The more concrete the message, the more useful the answer.
translations.contact-page.sent.title: Your message is on its way
translations.contact-page.sent.body: We read every message ourselves. Expect a reply within one working day, at the address you gave.
translations.contact-page.field.name: Your name
translations.contact-page.field.subject: What about
translations.contact-page.form.note: We use your address to reply, and for nothing else.
translations.contact-page.faq.title: Asked before you
translations.contact-page.cta.title: Or skip the conversation
translations.contact-page.cta.body: Creating a project and seeing what IDEM produces costs nothing, and takes about as long as writing this message.
translations.contact-page.channel.email.label: Email
translations.contact-page.channel.email.detail: The fastest route. A founder reads it.
translations.contact-page.channel.phone.label: Phone and WhatsApp
translations.contact-page.channel.office.label: Office
translations.contact-page.channel.office.detail: Come by if you are in town — tell us first.
translations.contact-page.channel.code.label: Issues and code
translations.contact-page.channel.code.detail: A bug or a feature request belongs here, in the open.
translations.contact-page.faq.delay.question: How long until someone replies?
translations.contact-page.faq.delay.answer: One working day for a written message. If it is urgent, call the number above — it rings on a founder's phone.
translations.contact-page.faq.enterprise.question: Can IDEM run inside my company?
translations.contact-page.faq.enterprise.answer: Yes. The licence lets you install the whole platform on your own servers, for your own company. Tell us your constraints and we will say what it takes.
translations.contact-page.faq.payment.question: How do I pay from my country?
translations.contact-page.faq.payment.answer: Mobile Money in thirteen African countries, or card. The wallet is topped up in CFA francs and spent as you generate.
translations.contact-page.faq.support.question: What help comes with a paid plan?
translations.contact-page.faq.support.answer: Written support by email, priority on paid plans, and the documentation. Nothing is hidden behind a support contract.
translations.contact-page.faq.reseller.question: I build sites for clients. Can I resell IDEM?
translations.contact-page.faq.reseller.answer: Agencies and consultants work with us already. Write with the kind of clients you serve and we will set the terms together.
translations.contact-page.error.incomplete: Name, email, subject and message are needed before we can reply.
translations.contact-page.error.network: The message did not go through. Try again, or write straight to contact@idem.africa.
translations.ideploy-page.hero.lede: You write the code. iDeploy puts it online, gives it a secure web address, backs it up and watches it. Nothing to install, not a single command to type.
translations.ideploy-page.steps.title: Four steps, once
translations.ideploy-page.steps.body: After that, every change to your code ships on its own.
translations.ideploy-page.where.title: Our servers, or yours
translations.ideploy-page.where.lede: The same product either way. What changes is who owns the machine, and where your data sleeps.
translations.ideploy-page.guard.title: Protected and watched
translations.ideploy-page.guard.lede: Everything switches on from the interface. You never touch the server.
translations.ideploy-page.domain.title: An address people recognise
translations.ideploy-page.domain.lede: Every app gets a working {$START_TAG_STRONG}.idem.africa{$CLOSE_TAG_STRONG} address the moment it goes live, with its certificate. Point your own domain at it when you are ready — the interface walks you through it, registrar by registrar.
translations.ideploy-page.domain.body: HTTPS is issued and renewed for you. There is no certificate to buy, upload or remember to replace.
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.title: The software your team already knows, installed in one click
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.lede: WordPress, Odoo, n8n, Supabase, Nextcloud, Grafana: the open-source tools millions of teams run. iDeploy installs them on our servers or on yours, with an address and backups.
translations.ideploy-page.also.title: And also
translations.ideploy-page.price.title: Your first app is on us
translations.ideploy-page.price.lede: The free plan is enough for a real project in production, commercial use included. You pay the day you need more.
translations.ideploy-page.price.paid: Paid plans start at 2 999 F per month. Mobile Money accepted, no card required.
translations.ideploy-page.around.title: Where the code comes from
translations.ideploy-page.around.body: iDeploy hosts whatever you give it. If you have not written it yet, the rest of IDEM does that part.
translations.ideploy-page.step.connect.title: Connect your code
translations.ideploy-page.step.connect.description: From GitHub, GitLab or a Dockerfile. An app built with iCode arrives without any of that.
translations.ideploy-page.step.where.title: Choose where it runs
translations.ideploy-page.step.where.description: Our servers, or yours. The same product either way, and the choice can change later.
translations.ideploy-page.step.guard.title: Tick what you need
translations.ideploy-page.step.guard.description: Firewall, vulnerability scans, backups. Each one is a switch in the interface, not a config file.
translations.ideploy-page.step.live.title: It is live
translations.ideploy-page.step.live.description: A web address and its certificate, in under a minute. Every push after that deploys on its own.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.idem.title: IDEM infrastructure
translations.ideploy-page.fork.idem.description: You look after nothing. We pick the machine, maintain it and replace it if it fails.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.idem.care: Updates, security and replacement after a failure: ours.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.idem.data: Hosted on IDEM infrastructure, under your plan.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.idem.fit: You want it to run without thinking about it.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.own.title: Your own server
translations.ideploy-page.fork.own.description: Plug your VPS in once with an SSH key. iDeploy installs it, secures it and keeps it current.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.own.machine: Your VPS, plugged in once with an SSH key. No server yet? iDeploy rents one for you.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.own.care: iDeploy installs it, secures it and keeps it current.
translations.ideploy-page.fork.own.fit: You already have a server, or your data has to stay with you.
translations.ideploy-page.guard.firewall.title: Firewall and WAF
translations.ideploy-page.guard.firewall.description: Block an address or a whole country, throttle the request rate, from the interface.
translations.ideploy-page.guard.scans.title: Scans before release
translations.ideploy-page.guard.scans.description: Code quality and known vulnerabilities are checked on every build. If the check fails, nothing ships.
translations.ideploy-page.guard.monitoring.title: Monitoring
translations.ideploy-page.guard.monitoring.descriptio: Requests, CPU, memory and disk, read continuously for your apps and your servers.
translations.ideploy-page.guard.alerts.title: Alerts where you already talk
translations.ideploy-page.guard.alerts.description: When something breaks, the message arrives in the channel your team is already in.
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.site.title: Website and content
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.business.title: Running the business
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.ai.title: AI and automation
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.backend.title: Your app's back end
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.monitor.title: Measuring and monitoring
translations.ideploy-page.catalogue.learning.title: Training
translations.ideploy-page.extra.database.title: Databases in one click
translations.ideploy-page.extra.database.description: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis and four more engines, backed up automatically.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.workspace.title: Workspaces
translations.ideploy-page.extra.workspace.description: Your site, API and database on a private network, reachable by name.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.preview.title: Preview environments
translations.ideploy-page.extra.preview.description: A test address per pull request, removed when it is merged.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.rollback.title: Rollback
translations.ideploy-page.extra.rollback.description: An earlier version goes back online in one click.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.terminal.title: A terminal in the browser
translations.ideploy-page.extra.terminal.description: A session on the server or inside the container, with no SSH client to set up.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.env.title: Variables picked up
translations.ideploy-page.extra.env.description: Read from your .env.example and shared across projects.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.cron.title: Scheduled tasks and volumes
translations.ideploy-page.extra.cron.description: A command on a schedule, and files that survive deployments.
translations.ideploy-page.extra.team.title: Team
translations.ideploy-page.extra.team.description: Invitations, roles and variables shared across the team.
translations.ideploy-page.free.domain: A .idem.africa address, plus one custom domain with HTTPS
translations.ideploy-page.ecosystem.icode.description: Describe the site or the application you need and it gets written, then handed straight to iDeploy.
translations.ideploy-page.ecosystem.idem.name: The IDEM platform
translations.ideploy-page.ecosystem.idem.description: Brand, business plan, finances and legal papers — the business the application belongs to.
translations.idev-page.hero.lede: Describe what you need in your own words. iCode writes the React code, runs it in front of you in the browser, and keeps changing it as you talk. The source code is yours to export.
translations.idev-page.targets.title: Three things it can build
translations.idev-page.steps.title: How a session goes
translations.idev-page.steps.body: There is no project setup, no repository to create and no build to configure. The first message is the first step.
translations.idev-page.preview.title: It runs while it is being written
translations.idev-page.preview.lede: The project runs in your browser — Node, the dev server and a real database, with nothing installed on your machine.
translations.idev-page.ship.title: Online in one move, or gone with you
translations.idev-page.ship.lede: « Put it online » hands the project to iDeploy and gives you an address — a static site or a full stack with its database, no GitHub account required. Or export the folder and host it wherever you like.
translations.idev-page.around.title: What comes before and after
translations.idev-page.around.body: iCode writes the application. The rest of the business — the brand, the plan, the address, the hosting — is the rest of IDEM.
translations.idev-page.target.site.title: A showcase site
translations.idev-page.target.site.description: Pages that present your business and bring in enquiries. Built from your brand if you already made one with IDEM.
translations.idev-page.target.web.title: A web application
translations.idev-page.target.web.description: Accounts, forms, a database, pages that do work. The kind of tool you would otherwise run on a spreadsheet.
translations.idev-page.target.mobile.title: A phone application
translations.idev-page.target.mobile.description: Laid out for a phone, installable straight from its link, and packaged for Android and iOS from the same code.
translations.idev-page.step.describe.title: Say what you need
translations.idev-page.step.describe.description: Plain sentences, in French or English. « A booking page for my salon, with the opening hours and a deposit » is enough to start.
translations.idev-page.step.build.title: Watch it get written
translations.idev-page.step.build.description: Files appear one after another and the preview reloads as they land. You can read every line while it happens.
translations.idev-page.step.adjust.title: Change it by talking
translations.idev-page.step.adjust.description: « Move the price above the photo », « add a second language ». No file to find, no code to edit by hand unless you want to.
translations.idev-page.step.ship.title: Put it online
translations.idev-page.step.ship.description: One button hands the project to iDeploy and returns a working address with HTTPS. Or export the source and host it yourself.
translations.idev-page.preview.container.title: Node runs in the tab
translations.idev-page.preview.container.description: The dev server starts inside your browser. Nothing to install, and the preview is the real project rather than a picture of it.
translations.idev-page.preview.database.title: A real database in the preview
translations.idev-page.preview.database.description: Postgres runs alongside the app, so sign-up, saved records and queries work before anything is deployed.
translations.idev-page.preview.fullstack.title: Front and back together
translations.idev-page.preview.fullstack.description: A full-stack project runs its interface and its API side by side, the way it will run in production.
translations.idev-page.preview.errors.title: Errors come with a fix
translations.idev-page.preview.errors.description: When the build or the page breaks, the error is shown with a « Fix » button that hands it back to the model with the stack trace.
translations.idev-page.preview.phone.title: A phone frame for phone apps
translations.idev-page.preview.phone.description: Mobile projects preview inside an iPhone and an Android mockup, because a phone layout cannot be judged in a desktop window.
translations.idev-page.preview.code.title: The code is not hidden
translations.idev-page.preview.code.description: Open the editor, read any file, edit it directly. The conversation and the editor work on the same project.
translations.idev-page.ecosystem.idem.name: The IDEM platform
translations.idev-page.ecosystem.idem.description: Brand, business plan, finances, legal papers and communication — everything the application is the front of.
translations.idev-page.ecosystem.ideploy.description: Hosting, domain name, certificates and logs, on our machines or on yours.
translations.open-source-page.hero.lede: The whole platform is published under Apache 2.0 with the Commons Clause. Read it, fork it, run it on your own machine, build for your clients with it. None of that needs our permission.
translations.open-source-page.license.title: Apache 2.0, in plain words
translations.open-source-page.license.body: Four rights the licence grants you, and the one obligation it puts on you. The full text ships with the repository.
translations.open-source-page.data.title: Where your work actually sits
translations.open-source-page.data.lede: Three places, and you pick. The platform does not change behaviour depending on which one you choose.
translations.open-source-page.law.title: No lock-in to argue about
translations.open-source-page.law.lede: Every deliverable leaves as a file you own: the brand book as a PDF, the logo and its variants as a ZIP, the generated site and app as source code. What the platform keeps, and for how long, is written down — not described in a sales page.
translations.open-source-page.community.title: Decisions happen in the open
translations.open-source-page.community.body: The roadmap, the issues and the arguments are public. If a choice affects how your business runs, you get to be in the conversation.
translations.open-source-page.cta.title: Clone it, or just use it
translations.open-source-page.cta.body: Running IDEM yourself costs you a server. Running it here costs nothing until you keep something.
translations.open-source-page.clause.read.title: Read and audit all of it
translations.open-source-page.clause.read.description: Every line of the platform is public, including how your data is stored and which model handles which request.
translations.open-source-page.clause.host.title: Install it on your own servers

translations.simulation.cta.title: Put your project under strain
translations.simulation.cta.body: Before you commit your time and your money, find out under what conditions your business can work and what could make it fail.
translations.simulation.entry.title: Two ways to start
translations.simulation.entry.project.title: From an IDEM project
translations.simulation.entry.project.body: Business plan, market analysis, financial forecasts and business model are already there. The engine has less to ask for, and you pay less.
translations.simulation.entry.import.title: By importing your business plan
translations.simulation.entry.import.body: PDF, DOCX or plain text. IDEM extracts the activity, market, target customer, prices and costs, then lets you fill in the gaps before you start.
translations.simulation.offers.title: What you are buying
translations.simulation.offers.body: Simulation is billed separately from the rest of IDEM: it spends external research, several agents and compute. The amount is shown and confirmed before anything starts.
translations.simulation.offers.run.name: Simulation
translations.simulation.offers.run.body: The scenarios, the deciding factors, the major risks and the viability index.
translations.simulation.offers.pack.name: Simulation + report
translations.simulation.offers.pack.body: The simulation and its full report, cheaper than buying both separately.
translations.simulation.offers.report.name: Full report
translations.simulation.offers.report.body: The detailed analysis and recommendations, for a simulation you already ran.
translations.simulation.evidence.title: Every figure says where it came from
translations.simulation.evidence.body: Observed data, a derived estimate and an assumption are not worth the same. Blurring them would give a false impression of precision.
translations.simulation.evidence.data.label: Data
translations.simulation.evidence.data.body: An observed, published figure with its source and its date. Fuel prices, urban density, exchange rates.
translations.simulation.evidence.estimate.label: Estimate
translations.simulation.evidence.estimate.body: A value derived from comparable data, when nothing direct exists for your market.
translations.simulation.evidence.assumption.label: Assumption
translations.simulation.evidence.assumption.body: A deliberate choice by the engine, flagged as such, because no reliable data was available.
translations.simulation.wall.title: A business does not run on five variables
translations.simulation.wall.body: It runs on dozens, sometimes hundreds of factors, and they are never quite the same from one project to the next.
translations.simulation.wall.badge.label: factors typically identified on a single project, before a single scenario is run.
translations.simulation.wall.more: and many more, depending on your sector
translations.simulation.hero.title: Test your business before you {$START_TAG_SPAN}launch{$CLOSE_TAG_SPAN} it
translations.simulation.hero.description: An idea can look excellent on paper and still fail once it meets the market. IDEM looks for the factors that can genuinely influence your business, simulates several possible futures, and shows you where your model breaks.
translations.simulation.fan.title: Fan of simulated trajectories
translations.simulation.fan.desc: From a single project, the engine lets many trajectories diverge. A minority stay above the viability threshold; most fall below it.
translations.simulation.honesty.title: What IDEM Simulator does not promise you
translations.simulation.honesty.p1: The results are estimates based on the data, assumptions and scenarios available at the time of analysis.
translations.simulation.honesty.p2: A high index guarantees neither viability, nor profitability, nor the long-term survival of your business. A low index does not mean the project is impossible: it means that, in the scenarios that were run, some factors carry significant risk.
translations.simulation.honesty.p3: It is a decision-support tool. Not a prediction, not a guarantee.
translations.simulation.loop.title: A simulation is not an endpoint
translations.simulation.loop.body: Change your price, your target customer or your funding in IDEM, run it again, and compare the two versions. What moves is not your chance of succeeding: it is how much strain your model takes.
translations.simulation.loop.caption: Each new run is kept, so you can compare versions instead of arguing about them.
translations.simulation.how.title: What IDEM does when you start a simulation
translations.simulation.how.body: This is not a conversation with an AI. It is a five-stage analysis.
translations.simulation.how.card.body: Several agents work in parallel: one reads the project, others research external data, another combines them into scenarios.
translations.simulation.pipeline.read.title: Reading the project
translations.simulation.pipeline.read.body: IDEM builds a structured picture of your project, separating what it knows from what it has to research, what stays uncertain, and what is missing.
translations.simulation.pipeline.discover.title: Factor discovery
translations.simulation.pipeline.discover.body: Agents look for the factors that can actually move this particular business, then rank them as critical, important, secondary or uncertain.
translations.simulation.pipeline.research.title: Data research
translations.simulation.pipeline.research.body: Prices, density, costs, regulation, seasonality: every external value arrives with its source, its date and how much confidence it carries.
translations.simulation.pipeline.simulate.title: Simulation
translations.simulation.pipeline.simulate.body: The engine combines factors and runs baseline, favourable and adverse scenarios, stress tests, and rare compound shocks.
translations.simulation.pipeline.analyse.title: Analysis
translations.simulation.pipeline.analyse.body: Viability index, robustness, confidence level, breaking points, the conditions viability depends on, and recommendations ranked by priority.
translations.simulation.readout.title: An index, never on its own
translations.simulation.readout.body: An index of 72 backed by solid data and an index of 72 riddled with uncertainty do not mean the same thing. IDEM always shows both together.
translations.simulation.readout.robustness.def: How well the model keeps holding as the factors deteriorate.
translations.simulation.readout.confidence.def: The quality of the data the analysis rests on, assumptions included.
translations.simulation.readout.uncertainties.def: What the simulation could not establish, and what still has to be checked on the ground.
translations.simulation.readout.card.label: Simulated viability index
translations.simulation.readout.card.caveat: This index measures how robust the project is across the scenarios that were run. It is not a prediction of success.
translations.simulation.report.title: The report answers one question
translations.simulation.report.body: What could make this project succeed or fail, and what should I change?
translations.simulation.report.note: Not "improve your marketing". Rather: acquisition cost is the model's main weakness, test an organic channel before raising the ad budget. Expected impact high, priority critical, confidence medium.

translations.simulation.report.caption: The report is delivered inside your project, next to the deliverables it was built from.
translations.simulation.report.s4: Scenarios, stress tests and extreme cases
translations.simulation.report.s10: What to validate in the real world

translations.simulation.sectors.body: Two businesses, two worlds. A fixed list of twenty variables applied to everyone would describe neither of them properly.

translations.simulation.stress.body: IDEM deliberately puts your business through hard situations, then tells you which ones it cannot take.
translations.simulation.stress.verdict.label: Verdict: no-go
translations.simulation.stress.verdict.body: When the conditions are genuinely bad, the engine says so, and lists exactly which scenarios the model could not survive.
translations.simulation.stress.q1: What happens if your main competitor cuts prices by 30%?
translations.simulation.stress.q2: What happens if your acquisition cost rises by 40%?

translations.simTerms.subtitle: Terms of Use for IDEM Simulation — business viability simulation
translations.simTerms.nav.project_creation: 7. THE PROJECT CREATED FROM YOUR PLAN
translations.simTerms.scope.title: 1. WHAT THESE TERMS COVER
translations.simTerms.scope.content: These terms apply to IDEM Simulation, the part of IDEM that puts a business project under stress and returns a viability index, scenarios, factors and a report. They come in addition to the IDEM Terms of Service and to the Privacy Policy, which continue to apply. Where a point is specific to simulation, this document prevails. You are asked to accept these terms before each run, because each run reads your project and sends an extract of it to artificial intelligence models.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.title: 2. WHAT A SIMULATION IS
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.content: A run proceeds in six stages: reading your project or your business plan, discovering the factors that could move it, gathering the external figures it can, building a numeric model, running scenarios on that model, and analysing what came out. The arithmetic is deterministic — the same figures always produce the same projection. What surrounds it is not: the choice of factors, the design of the scenarios and every written commentary are produced by AI models, which can be wrong.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.baseline: The whole model rests on around ten figures — price, variable cost, fixed costs, acquisition cost, growth, retention, starting capital. Where your project does not state one, the engine estimates it and says so.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.states: Every element is presented with its status: read in your source, to be researched, estimated, or missing. That distinction is part of the result and must not be dropped when the result is passed on.
translations.simTerms.what_it_is.confidence: Every run carries a confidence level. A high viability index resting on assumptions is not the same claim as the same index resting on established data.
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.title: 3. WHAT A SIMULATION IS NOT
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.content: A simulation is a decision-support tool. It describes what happens to a model under the scenarios studied. It does not tell you whether your business will succeed or fail, and no figure it produces should be read as a forecast of your actual revenue, profitability or funding.
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.warning.title: A viability index is not a promise
translations.simTerms.not_a_prediction.warning.conten: The index measures how robust a model is across the scenarios that were run, on the figures that were available. It is not a probability of success, not a valuation, and not a guarantee of any outcome. Decisions you take on the strength of a run — investing, hiring, borrowing, launching or abandoning — remain entirely yours.
translations.simTerms.no_advice.title: 4. NOT PROFESSIONAL ADVICE
translations.simTerms.no_advice.content: Nothing produced by IDEM Simulation — index, scenarios, factors, risks, recommendations, report — constitutes financial, investment, accounting, tax, legal or regulatory advice. IDEM is not a financial adviser, an auditor, an accountant or a law firm, and no client relationship of that kind arises from your use of the service. Before acting on a run, and in particular before presenting one to a bank, an investor or an administration, have it reviewed by a qualified professional in your jurisdiction.
translations.simTerms.your_document.title: 5. YOUR BUSINESS PLAN
translations.simTerms.your_document.content: You may import a business plan in PDF, Word (.docx) or Markdown. Here is what happens to it, stated plainly so that you know what you are agreeing to:
translations.simTerms.your_document.extraction: The text is extracted from your file. The file itself is not kept after the reading; a scanned document that yields no text is refused.
translations.simTerms.your_document.screening: The text is screened without any AI call. A document that has nothing of a business plan is refused at that point, and nothing of it is sent anywhere.
translations.simTerms.your_document.condensation: Only an extract of the informative passages — on the order of fourteen thousand characters — is sent to the models. Your document is not transmitted in full.
translations.simTerms.your_document.cache: The reading produced from that extract is cached for up to seven days, keyed on a fingerprint of the document, so that re-importing the same file costs nothing. It is attached to your account and to no one else's.
translations.simTerms.your_document.retention: What is kept afterwards is the reading — the profile, the figures, the knowledge items — inside the project it created, under your account, for as long as you keep that project.
translations.simTerms.ai_processing.title: 6. PROCESSING BY AI MODELS
translations.simTerms.ai_processing.content: Running a simulation sends an extract of your project or of your business plan to third-party artificial intelligence providers acting as processors for IDEM. The categories of provider and the safeguards that apply are described in the Privacy Policy, which you also accept before each run. If your plan contains information you are not willing to have processed in that way — personal data of third parties, trade secrets belonging to someone else, information covered by a confidentiality undertaking — remove it before importing.
translations.simTerms.project_creation.title: 7. THE PROJECT CREATED FROM YOUR PLAN
translations.simTerms.project_creation.content: An imported business plan belongs to no existing project, so launching a run creates one in IDEM on your behalf, populated from what the reading yielded: name, description, sector, targets, constraints, budget, and the contact and team details written in your document. That project is yours. It appears in your workspace like any other, it can be edited, and deleting it removes what the reading had stored.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.title: 8. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.content: By launching a run you confirm that:
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.rights: You hold the rights to the document you import, or the authorisation to submit it for processing.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.third_par: You have removed, or are entitled to submit, any personal data of third parties it contains.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.accuracy: The figures you supply, including the answers you give to fill the gaps the engine reports, are yours. A run built on wrong inputs produces a wrong result, and the engine cannot detect that.
translations.simTerms.your_responsibilities.presentat: If you pass a result on to a third party, you keep with it the confidence level and the uncertainties attached to it.

translations.simTerms.billing.content: Simulation is billed separately from the rest of IDEM, because a run spends external research, several agents and computation. translations.simulation.faq.q1.question: Does IDEM Simulator predict whether my business will succeed?
translations.simulation.faq.q1.answer: No. The results are estimates based on the data, assumptions and scenarios available at the time of analysis. A high index guarantees neither viability nor profitability, and a low index does not mean the project is impossible.
translations.simulation.faq.q2.question: Do I need to have built my project in IDEM to run a simulation?
translations.simulation.faq.q2.answer: No. You can import an existing business plan as PDF, DOCX or plain text: IDEM extracts the activity, market, business model, prices and costs. Projects already built in IDEM get a reduced price, because the deliverables are already available.
translations.simulation.faq.q3.question: What does the simulated viability index measure?
translations.simulation.faq.q3.answer: It measures how robust the model is across the scenarios that were run: how well it keeps holding as the factors deteriorate. It is always shown together with a confidence level and the list of main uncertainties.
translations.simulation.faq.q4.question: Is simulation included in IDEM?
translations.simulation.faq.q4.answer: No, it is billed separately because it spends external research, several agents and compute. The amount is shown and confirmed before the run starts. The full report can be bought with the simulation or later.
